title: Contextual Compact Rail and Smart Collapse for Table UX
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Large, virtualized tables in the Console are hard to scan at high density. Users frequently need to hide low-importance columns, temporarily reduce column width, or surface important columns without leaving flow. This ticket proposes a lightweight, contextual UI — the 'compact rail' — that appears when interacting with a table row/header to let users snap columns to mini widths, temporarily collapse groups, and toggle density presets. The feature must be keyboard-first, performant with virtualization, and provide telemetry for evaluating effectiveness.

Goals:
- Reduce horizontal cognitive load on wide tables while preserving discoverability of hidden data.
- Support rapid transient adjustments (snap-to-mini, quick collapse) without changing persistent column layout unless explicitly saved.
- Work within existing virtualized rendering (windowing) to avoid forcing full reflows.
- Ensure accessibility (screen reader announcements, keyboard toggles, focus management).

Deliverables:
- High-fidelity Figma screens for hover/keyboard rail, column snapshots, and collapse animations.
- Interaction spec (timing, thresholds, keyboard shortcuts, ARIA roles).
- Exportable tokens and spacing for compact/dense presets.
- Engineering tickets (rendering optimization and telemetry).
- A/B plan to measure time-to-find and column toggle frequency.
comments: 2025-02-25 - Ava Chen: Initial discovery notes from interviews with three platform teams. Main pain points: accidental horizontal scrolling, mental model mismatch between temporary and persistent column changes, and poor discoverability of density presets.

2025-02-27 - Marcus Patel: Added two alternative interaction patterns to Figma: (A) hover-rail with contextual icons; (B) keyboard-anchored rail that appears on focus of header cell. Prefer keyboard-anchored for accessibility but keep hover for mouse-first flows.

2025-02-28 - Design Review: Feedback from Sofia (PM) and Luis (Engineering). Luis flagged potential virtualization conflict: snapping a column to mini width can change measured cell sizes and break the virtualization buffer. Action: coordinate with ENG-59210 for safe measurement protocol and avoid layout thrash by using CSS transforms where possible.

2025-03-01 - Accessibility review: Add aria-live region updates when a column collapses or expands, provide a single-key toggle (.). Map focus trap behavior so keyboard users can open the rail, use arrow keys to change collapse state, then ESC to close. Ensure SR reads out the column priority label when collapsed.

2025-03-02 - Prototype test (internal): 6 designers and SEs tested the hover-rail. Observations: hover-rail is discoverable on large screens but is easy to miss on compact windows; keyboard anchor found by power users and is faily discoverable with a short tip. Need onboarding micro-copy. Recorded session linked in Confluence.

2025-03-03 - Marcus Patel: Updated interaction spec to prefer non-layout-changing animations for the first iteration. Engineers to implement visual mini-width using clip-path + transform to avoid reflow. Created ENG dependency: ENG-59888 (virtualization-safe collapse API).
2025-03-03 - Sofia (PM): Approved moving to implementation spike pending ENG-59888. We're tracking customer-impact as 'medium' — expected to improve power-user efficiency on large tenant dashboards.

Next steps: Ship a small engineering spike (2w) to validate virtualization-safe visual collapse, then iterate on keyboard discovery and telemetry events. Prepare A/B test metrics: column-toggle rate, average horizontal scroll distance per session, and time-to-first-find for key columns.
